proof:
# A concrete halfspace-dominated target for one integer variable

Let C be a convex body in R x R^d with finitely many positive-volume integer fibers, and let mu_0 denote its unnormalized mixed volume, of total mass M. Fix an integer k whose marginal weight is a weighted median. Write L and R for the restrictions of mu_0 to integer fibers strictly to the left and strictly to the right of k, and let their total masses be A and B. Write c=vol_d(C_k). Thus A+B+c=M and A,B<=M/2.

There is a probability measure nu supported on the single fiber C_k such that

`nu(H) <= 2 mu_0(H)/M`

for every closed ambient halfspace H, including oblique ones.

If either A or B vanishes, then c>=M/2, so the normalized uniform law on C_k works. Otherwise let X and Y be independent with laws L/A and R/B. Write their integer coordinates as p<k<q. Define

`Z = ((q-k)/(q-p)) X + ((k-p)/(q-p)) Y`.

Its integer coordinate is exactly k; convexity ensures Z belongs to C_k. Let P be its probability law. Define the unnormalized target

`eta = vol_d restricted to C_k + min(A,B) P`.

For every closed halfspace H, if Z is in H then at least one of X,Y is in H. Consequently

`eta(H) <= mu_0(C_k intersect H) + min(A,B)(L(H)/A + R(H)/B) <= mu_0(H)`.

Its total mass is

`W=c+min(A,B)=M-max(A,B)>=M/2`.

Therefore `nu=eta/W` has the asserted domination. This construction is deterministic at the level of probability laws: it uses the explicitly specified product coupling, not the assertion that a random center works.

For finite collections of left and right fibers, P is a finite positive mixture of pushforwards of products of uniform convex-body laws. Each component has a log-concave density (a scaled convolution), but their sum with the uniform central-fiber density is not asserted to be log-concave. No sharp depth bound for this mixture has been established.

## Exact finite cover consequence

Let H_1,...,H_N be ambient halfspaces and let lambda_i>=0 satisfy

`sum_i lambda_i 1_{H_i}(k,x) >= 1` for all x in C_k.

Integrating against eta proves the concrete dual inequality

`sum_i lambda_i mu_0(H_i) >= W >= M/2`.

Thus no finite weighted halfspace-cover certificate can obstruct an *arbitrary* probability target on a median fiber in the one-integer-variable case. Any obstruction to a log-concave target must use log-concavity, not just measure feasibility.

## The hard-volume range for three fibers

For three fibers of respective volumes a,c,b, with a>=b and the middle fiber selected, the construction has mass W=c+b. It provides a uniform target immediately if c>=M/2, or if either endpoint itself has mass >=M/2 and is selected instead. The remaining volume range is

`a<c+b`, `c<a+b`, with W-M/2=(c+b-a)/2`.

Near a=c+b the measure-domination slack can be arbitrarily small, although convexity also imposes the exact Brunn-Minkowski restriction

`c^(1/d) >= (a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))/2`.

This range is the appropriate place to test the stronger demand for a log-concave target. The construction itself does not supply such a target and does not resolve OC.
